To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. the trans-Plankian problem of inflationary cosmology is not solved by the assumption that fluctuations exit the Hubble-radius in their local vacuum-state; 2. the back-reaction from fluctuations is not negligible and can affect the background in important ways.

(i) in the absence of a mechanism to generate a local vacuum state for cosmological perturbation modes at early times, the inflationary prediction for the power spectrum of cosmological perturbatons is not reliable, and (ii) the backreaction of fluctuations on the background evolution is important and cannot be neglected.
the spectrum of perturbations in a contracting phase is red, and back-reaction effects limit the duration of the deflationary phase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physics of inflation and the trans-Planckiian problem.
the question of how to understand cosmological perturbative fluctuations on the basis of a theory of quantum gravity.
the question of how much of the physics of inflation can be understood in a model-independent way, and how much depends on the physics of the Planck era.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
inflationary cosmology needs to be understood in the context of a complete theory of the universe.
the standard inflationary cosmological scenario is not viable in its present form.
, in order to have a successful inflationary model, it is necessary to understand the physics at Planckian energy scales and the dynamics of the contracting phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the trans-Plankian problem is not a technical problem, it is a conceptual problem for cosmology.
the inflationary paradigm needs a new foundation, and the trans-Plankian problem and back-reaction are two important issues which must be addressed.
the inflationary universe model should be modified to incorporate a non-singular phase of contraction, which is followed by deflation and inflation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a full treatment of inflationary cosmology must take into account the trans-Planickian problem and the effects of back-reaction.
the trans-Planockian problem is a serious issue for the theory of inflationary cosmology and cannot be ignored.
, in a model in which a period of contraction preceded the inflationary phase, the spectrum of cosmological perturbatins is highly non-trivial.
